# Module 1 Quality Baseline

*Generated by `tools/profile_image_quality.py` on 2026-09-11 — 380 images sampled across four corpora.*

Phase 1 prep. The README specifies **which** quality metrics Module 1 computes
but not what counts as a reject. These are the measured distributions the
thresholds in [`config/quality_thresholds.json`](../config/quality_thresholds.json)
come from.

---

## 1. The resolution-dependence problem, measured

[datasets.md](datasets.md) §6 claimed that a sharpness metric in raw pixel
units is resolution-dependent and will mis-score across corpora.

**This must be tested *within* a corpus, not pooled across all four.** Pooling
confounds resolution with dataset identity — DRIVE is simultaneously the
smallest and the sharpest corpus, so a pooled correlation mostly measures
"which dataset is this". The clean test is a corpus with wide internal
resolution variety and constant content: **APTOS**, which spans 640×480 to
2588×1958.

Correlation of each sharpness metric against FOV diameter, per corpus:

| Corpus | FOV diameter range | r (raw) | r (FOV-normalised) |
|---|---|---|---|
| APTOS | 551–3617 px | -0.746 | -0.466 |
| IDRiD | 3408–4144 px | -0.137 | +0.235 |  *(near-constant resolution — uninformative)*
| DRIVE | 551–576 px | +0.318 | +0.328 |  *(near-constant resolution — uninformative)*
| Messidor2 | 911–2254 px | -0.367 | -0.213 |

*(Pooled across all corpora: raw `-0.267`, normalised `-0.304` — confounded, shown only for completeness.)*

**Verdict.** Within APTOS, raw Laplacian variance correlates with FOV
diameter at `-0.746` — the metric is measuring image size about as
much as it measures focus. Rescaling to a canonical FOV diameter cuts that
to `-0.466`.

So normalisation is **necessary but not sufficient**. A residual
correlation of `0.47` still means a threshold tuned on
small images will mis-fire on large ones. Module 1 should either band the
threshold by FOV diameter, or use a focus measure that is genuinely
scale-invariant (e.g. energy ratio across a fixed band of spatial
frequencies relative to FOV diameter, rather than a fixed-size kernel).

Median sharpness by FOV-diameter band (APTOS), showing the effect concretely:

| FOV diameter | n | raw | normalised |
|---|---|---|---|
| < 800 px | 12 | 35.3 | 23.3 |
| 800–1600 px | 46 | 53.5 | 46.5 |
| > 1600 px | 62 | 14.5 | 20.4 |

## 3. Derived thresholds

Written to [`config/quality_thresholds.json`](../config/quality_thresholds.json).
Percentiles are over the pooled sample:

| Check | Borderline | Reject |
|---|---|---|
| Sharpness (normalised) | below 16.28 | below 9.5 |
| Illumination CV | above 0.2437 | above 0.3412 |
| Glare fraction | above 0.03834 | above 0.29142 |
| FOV coverage | — | below 0.4485 |
| Contrast | — | below 46.58 |

> ⚠️ **These are calibrated on curated research datasets.** All four corpora
> were captured by trained operators on mounted cameras. Field images from
> handheld devices in a PHC will be substantially worse, so a threshold set at
> the 2nd percentile here will reject far more than 2% in deployment. The
> README's own risk table calls this out. Re-calibrate against deliberately
> degraded images (Phase 1's synthetic degradation task) before trusting the
> reject rate.
